subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Operations management is mainly concerned with:
options: Producing goods and services by converting inputs into outputs
questions.explain: Operations turns inputs (resources) into outputs (goods/services), adding value.
Job production makes single, bespoke items (e.g. a tailored suit).

options: Continuous production of large volumes of standardised goods
questions.explain: Flow production continuously makes large quantities of identical products.

questions.q: A bakery producing loaves in groups by type, switching between products, uses:
questions.explain: Batch production makes groups of identical items before switching to another batch.

options: Minimise stock by receiving inputs only as needed
questions.explain: JIT reduces stock-holding costs by receiving materials just as they are required.

questions.q: Quality assurance differs from quality control because assurance:
options: Builds quality into the whole process (prevention)
questions.explain: Quality assurance prevents defects throughout the process; quality control inspects output at the end.
Kaizen is the lean principle of continuous, incremental improvement.

questions.q: For a high-street retailer, a key location factor is:
questions.explain: Retailers prioritise being close to customers; manufacturers may prioritise costs or suppliers.

options: Bringing production back to the home country
questions.explain: Reshoring returns previously offshored production to the domestic country.

questions.q: Break-even output is calculated as fixed costs divided by:
questions.explain: Break-even quantity = fixed costs / contribution per unit.

questions.q: Fixed costs are £4,000 and contribution per unit is £8. The break-even output is:
questions.explain: 4,000 / 8 = 500 units to break even.
Margin of safety shows how far sales can fall before a loss is made.

options: Total revenue equals total costs (no profit or loss)
questions.explain: Break-even is where total revenue exactly covers total costs.

options: A minimum stock level held to avoid running out
questions.explain: Buffer stock guards against unexpected demand or supply delays.

questions.q: Capacity utilisation is calculated as (actual output ÷ maximum possible output) ×:
questions.explain: Capacity utilisation (%) shows how much of maximum capacity is being used.

options: Preparing in advance for possible future crises
questions.explain: Contingency planning prepares responses before a crisis; crisis management handles it as it happens.

options: An unexpected event requiring an immediate response
questions.explain: Crisis management responds to sudden, serious, unexpected events.
Patents protect inventions; trademarks protect brand identifiers; copyright protects creative works.

questions.q: Research and development (R&D) mainly contributes to:
options: Innovation and new or improved products
questions.explain: R&D drives innovation, creating new products/processes and competitive advantage.

questions.q: A management information system (MIS) helps managers by:
options: Providing data and information to support decisions
questions.explain: An MIS gathers and presents information to improve managerial decision-making.

options: Very large data sets analysed for insights
questions.explain: Big data involves analysing large, complex data sets to inform decisions.

options: Increasing the worth of inputs through the production process
questions.explain: Operations add value when outputs are worth more than the inputs used.
